checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.why: Output is still horizontal 858x480; duration about 10 s is kept.
Second clip uses heavy bold white sans with black outline and yellow highlight, much bigger than the thin serif in the first.

must.item: Complete speech accurately subtitled and synced
must.why: Visible captions match the expected text, but no caption is visible in the 1 s and 9.6 s frames, and audio sync can't be judged. 'Hi everyone!' is not seen.

must.item: Captions fit in vertical frame and clear of TikTok UI areas
must.why: No vertical frame. Captions sit mid-lower, centred, within the horizontal frame, and cover her hands and torso.

must.item: Face visible and undistorted, not obscured
must.why: Face is clear and natural in all frames and the captions sit below it.

must.item: Original voice preserved, no dub or music
must.why: Audio is present with the same peak level, but the content can't be heard.

exact_text.read_as: Not visible in any sampled frame; the 1 s frame has no caption.

exact_text.text: Today I want to show you
exact_text.read_as: Today I want to / show you three easy
three easy / ways (split across two caption cards)

exact_text.text: to make your mornings less stressful.
exact_text.read_as: ways to make your mornings less stressful.

faults.what: The video was not made vertical, which was an explicit request. The agent said so openly and told the user to crop it themselves.
The caption is in the lower-middle and covers her hands and sweater. It would collide with TikTok UI if the clip were made vertical.
The 'Hi everyone!' caption is not seen in the 1 s frame.
The yellow highlight is on a single word and jumps around ('you', 'your'). That is a style choice and acceptable.

summary: The captions are now big, bold and readable with the face intact, but the clip is still horizontal and not 9:16, so the main request is unmet.
